domains.label: Platform
domains.purpose: Run by Sakalya: plans, billing clinics, feature rollout, support, platform analytics. Console only.

domains.label: Identity
domains.purpose: People who sign in, their sessions and devices. One user can belong to many clinics.

domains.label: Clinic setup
domains.purpose: The clinic itself: branches, domains, rooms, modules, roles, staff memberships, numbering.

domains.label: Patients and doctors
domains.purpose: Each clinic's own patient records, identifiers, families, referral sources and practitioners.

domains.label: Scheduling
domains.purpose: Appointments, their history, and the walk-in token queue.

domains.label: Clinical
domains.purpose: Visits, notes, vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures, treatment plans, files and specialty data.

domains.label: Clinic operations
domains.purpose: Lab work, inventory and stock, equipment maintenance, payroll and consultant fees.

domains.label: Money
domains.purpose: Price list, bills, payments, refunds, expenses and daily cash closing.

domains.label: Notifications
domains.purpose: Templates, rules, consent, recalls, campaigns, promo codes, the outbox and every message sent.

domains.label: Websites
domains.purpose: Generated clinic websites, their versions, booking requests and traffic.

domains.label: Trust and audit
domains.purpose: Patient consents, who viewed what, every change, and data-rights requests.

domains.label: Onboarding
domains.purpose: First-login progress and data imports from old software.

tables.name: plans
tables.purpose: Subscription plans clinics can buy (Solo, Clinic, Pro, Enterprise).

tables.name: features
tables.purpose: Every feature that a plan can include or limit.

tables.name: plan_features
tables.purpose: What each plan includes, and its limits.
tables.notes: Primary key (plan_id, feature_id).

tables.name: subscriptions
tables.purpose: Which plan a clinic is on and whether it is paid up.

tables.name: saas_invoices
tables.purpose: Sakalya's own GST invoices to clinics for the subscription.

tables.name: entitlement_overrides
tables.purpose: Per-clinic exceptions to the plan: promos, grandfathering, custom deals.

tables.name: usage_counters
tables.purpose: How much of each limited feature a clinic used this month.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, feature_id, period). Incremented by the API and worker.

tables.name: feature_flags
tables.purpose: Switches that release a feature gradually, separate from plans.

tables.name: flag_rules
tables.purpose: Who a flag is on for: named clinics, a percentage, a plan, a platform or app version.

tables.name: platform_users
tables.purpose: Sakalya staff who can use the console, and their role.

tables.name: auth_handoffs
tables.purpose: Central sign-in: one-time codes that hand a session to one clinic or console host, valid 60 seconds.
tables.notes: Written and redeemed only through app.auth_handoff_create() and app.auth_handoff_redeem().

cols.name: code_hash
cols.note: unique, SHA-256 of the code; the code is never stored

cols.name: target_host
cols.note: the only host that may redeem it

cols.name: redeemed
cols.note: whether that attempt gave a session

tables.name: clinic_applications
tables.purpose: Clinics asking to join from the public landing page; staff approve or reject them in the console.
tables.notes: No grants: the API reaches it through definer functions only. Approval creates the clinic, the owner's invitation and the invitation email in one transaction.

cols.name: submissions
cols.note: times the address applied while pending

tables.name: support_grants
tables.purpose: Time-limited read access a clinic owner gives one named Sakalya staff member (support.grant).
tables.notes: Platform staff can't hold memberships (0172); a grant is their only way into a clinic. While active, app.support_authorize admits them on the clinic host through routes that name a permission, with read permissions only, actor kind support (the database refuses their writes in app.set_row_meta), and records each request in support_actions. A trigger allows one change: revocation. Ends by itself at ends_at.

cols.name: platform_user_id
cols.note: one named person, owner or support role

cols.name: reason
cols.note: 3 to 500 characters, shown to the staff member

tables.name: support_actions
tables.purpose: Every request Sakalya staff made under a support grant: the grant, method and route template.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, at, id), partitioned by month. Written by app.support_authorize only; the clinic reads its own rows (GET /support-grants/{id}/actions).

cols.name: route
cols.note: the route template, never a value

cols.name: request_id
cols.note: joins the change history and access record

tables.name: announcements
tables.purpose: Release notes and notices shown inside the clinic apps.

tables.name: org_daily_stats
tables.purpose: Per-clinic daily counts for the console. Counts only, never patient data.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, day). Written nightly, copied to BigQuery.

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Anyone who signs in: staff, doctors, patients, Sakalya staff.

tables.name: sessions
tables.purpose: Signed-in sessions, so a stolen phone or idle PC can be signed out.

tables.name: patient_sessions
tables.purpose: Patient app sign-in sessions, so a patient can see where they are signed in and sign one out.
tables.notes: Recorded by app.patient_access on every patient request, which also refuses a revoked session; GET /me/patient/sessions and DELETE /me/patient/sessions/{id}. Staff sessions stay in sessions (patient accounts are not users).

cols.name: provider_session_id
cols.note: session_id claim in the JWT, unique

tables.name: devices
tables.purpose: Phones and browsers a user signs in from, with push tokens.

tables.name: organizations
tables.purpose: A clinic business, the tenant. Everything clinic-owned points here.
tables.notes: Members can read only their own clinic's row. The console creates clinics through app.create_clinic().

cols.name: number_prefix
cols.note: 1 to 3 capital letters: SC in SC-1042

tables.name: branches
tables.purpose: Locations of a clinic. Single-location clinics have one.

cols.name: gstin
cols.note: when the branch has its own GST registration

cols.name: state_code
cols.note: GST state code, e.g. 27 for Maharashtra; the place of supply

tables.name: org_domains
tables.purpose: Host names that resolve to a clinic: its portal, its free website address (site) and its own domain (website).
tables.notes: Read before the clinic is known, through app.resolve_clinic_host(); cached in memory for a short time. New portal rows start pending (trigger); publishing a site writes its site row (app.site_host_publish); the outbox job makes hosts work and removes taken-down sites (app.edge_hosts_work).

cols.name: edge_status
cols.note: portal and site rows: pending, ready, failed, removing (a taken-down site)

cols.name: edge_next_attempt_at
cols.note: when the outbox job tries next

tables.name: slug_history
tables.purpose: Old slugs, so renamed clinics, doctors and pages keep redirecting.

tables.name: rooms
tables.purpose: Chairs, rooms and labs that appointments can be booked into.

tables.name: org_modules
tables.purpose: Specialty modules switched on for a clinic, with their settings.

cols.name: settings
cols.note: e.g. tooth numbering FDI or Universal

tables.name: org_settings
tables.purpose: One row per clinic: branding, bill and prescription settings, defaults.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id): exactly one row per clinic.

cols.name: booking
cols.note: online booking: enabled, slot_minutes, buffer_minutes, auto_confirm, horizon_days, min_notice_minutes

cols.name: patient_retention_years
cols.note: 7 to 50; null keeps the default 7 years

tables.name: assets
tables.purpose: Non-medical files: logos, signatures, generated PDFs, website images.
tables.notes: Stored in a different bucket from patient attachments.

tables.name: permissions
tables.purpose: Every permission the API checks, such as patients.read.
tables.notes: Seeded by migrations from the Rust permission list; a test checks that they match. intake.write (migration 0310: owner, doctor, front desk, assistant) records patient-reported allergies and "No known allergies" at a walk-in and grants no clinical reading.

cols.name: scopes
cols.note: which of all, own, assigned it can be narrowed to; always all

tables.name: role_templates
tables.purpose: Default roles copied into each new clinic: owner, doctor, front desk, assistant, finance.

tables.name: role_template_permissions
tables.purpose: The permissions each default role starts with.
tables.notes: Primary key (role_template_id, permission).

tables.name: roles
tables.purpose: Named bundles of permissions. Seeded from templates; owners can add their own.
tables.notes: Key unique among live roles. Only unused custom roles are removed; standard roles never are.

cols.name: key
cols.note: owner, doctor, consultant, finance, front_desk, assistant, or custom

cols.name: template_id
cols.note: the template a custom role started from

tables.name: role_changes
tables.purpose: Who changed a role's access and what it was before and after.

tables.name: role_permissions
tables.purpose: What a role may do: module.action plus a scope.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, role_id, permission).

cols.name: permission
cols.note: a key from permissions: patients.read, finance.view

tables.name: memberships
tables.purpose: A user's place in a clinic: role, branches, status. The link between users and clinics.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, user_id): one membership per person per clinic. Before the clinic scope is set it is read only through app.authorize(). At most one of avatar_preset and avatar_file_id; the member sets their own with PUT /me/avatar, and app.my_clinics returns both for the clinic switcher.

cols.name: avatar_preset
cols.note: the staff avatar as a preset id the apps ship (migration 0386)

cols.name: avatar_file_id
cols.note: or the member's own PNG or JPEG photo in file storage under the clinic's folder, read through signed links

cols.name: avatar_mime
cols.note: image/png or image/jpeg, set with avatar_file_id

tables.name: dashboard_layouts
tables.purpose: The Today board's layout: the clinic's default (no membership) and each member's own.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0605). One clinic row and one row per member (partial unique indexes). A member's layout wins, then the clinic's, then the MedSync template; a reset deletes the row. GET/PUT/DELETE /me/dashboard-layout and /settings/dashboard-layout (settings.manage). No patient data.

cols.name: layout
cols.note: versioned JSON v2: template, density, card, rail and widgets with zone, size and options; checked against the widget registry in aarogyam-domain

tables.name: membership_branches
tables.purpose: Which branches a staff member works at. No rows means every branch.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, membership_id, branch_id). Branch-scoped permissions read this table.

tables.name: invitations
tables.purpose: Pending invites to join a clinic.

tables.name: number_sequences
tables.purpose: Counters behind readable numbers: SC-1042, V-2026-0318, SC/26-27/000318.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, kind, series, period). app.next_number() issues a number with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING in the caller's transaction, so the first number of a new year needs no setup. GST invoice numbers stay within 16 characters.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: patient, visit, invoice, prescription, receipt, lab_order, queue_token

cols.name: series
cols.note: main, a separate series such as one per GSTIN, or a branch for queue tokens

cols.name: period
cols.note: financial year such as 26-27 or a local date for queue tokens, in the clinic's time zone; or empty

tables.name: patients
tables.purpose: A clinic's own record of a patient. Two clinics never share this row.
tables.notes: A phone number is contact information, never identity: families share numbers and numbers change. A merge only sets merged_into_id; records stay on the original patient and reads resolve to the canonical one, so a wrong merge can be undone. Number, phone and name-prefix search use plain indexes; fuzzy name search goes through app.search_patients(), because trigram matching can't use an index under row-level security. Same-phone registrations get a duplicate warning, never an automatic merge.

cols.name: number
cols.note: SC-1042, unique per clinic, used in URLs

cols.name: search_name
cols.note: lower-case name kept by a trigger, for prefix search

cols.name: birth_date_estimated
cols.note: date_of_birth was estimated from an age

cols.name: merged_into_id
cols.note: set by a merge, cleared by an unmerge

cols.name: allergies_reviewed
cols.note: unknown, none_known, has_allergies; set by walk-in intake and by recording an active allergy

cols.name: row_version
cols.note: starts at 1 and goes up when the record changes; sent as the ETag, checked against If-Match on edits

cols.name: erased_at
cols.note: set with status erased: a tombstone with identity cleared

tables.name: patient_identifiers
tables.purpose: Extra IDs for a patient: the clinic's file number, smart card, ABHA, legacy import.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, kind, value).

tables.name: family_links
tables.purpose: Relationships between patients in the same clinic: parent, child, spouse, guardian.

cols.name: can_manage
cols.note: guardian may act for this patient

tables.name: referral_sources
tables.purpose: Where patients come from, for the finance and marketing filters.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: patient, doctor, online, walk_in, camp, insurance, other

tables.name: medical_history_items
tables.purpose: Patient-level history: past conditions, surgeries, long-term medicines, habits, family history.

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: patient_accounts
tables.purpose: A person signed in to the patient app with a verified email. Holds no clinic data.
tables.notes: Made on the first patient-app request from the token's verified email. Reached only through definer functions (app.patient_access and friends, migration 0261); app_user has no grants.

tables.name: patient_links
tables.purpose: Connects a patient account to the clinic's record of that patient.
tables.notes: Never made automatically by phone or name. One open link per account per clinic, one active account per record. Every clinic table has a restrictive patient_account policy: a patient account reads only the linked record's appointments, issued prescriptions and bills, payments and shared files.

cols.name: linked_via
cols.note: code (a clinic-issued link code) or clinic_confirmed (a match the patient asked for and the clinic confirmed)

cols.name: consented_at
cols.note: when the patient redeemed the code or asked

tables.name: patient_link_codes
tables.purpose: Link codes from "Invite to patient app": shown as a QR code and emailed through the outbox.

cols.name: code_hash
cols.note: SHA-256 of the 10-character code; the code itself is never stored

cols.name: replaced_at
cols.note: a newer code for the same record

tables.name: practitioners
tables.purpose: Doctors who see patients at the clinic, with registration and fees.
tables.notes: Built in M3 with the columns the calendar needs. Planned: slug (public page), qualifications, council, signature_asset_id -> assets, default_fee_paise, is_visiting.

cols.name: membership_id
cols.note: null for a visiting consultant without a sign-in

tables.name: working_hours
tables.purpose: Weekly hours per clinic or doctor. Split shifts are two rows.
tables.notes: Replaced as a whole per doctor. Clinic opening hours are in clinic_hours. valid_from/valid_to are planned.

tables.name: clinic_hours
tables.purpose: When each branch of the clinic is open, by weekday. Split shifts are two rows.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0330). Replaced as a whole per branch (GET/PUT /clinic-hours). Chair utilization counts open minutes from it, nine hours a day when a branch has none. Clinics that existed got the union of their active doctors' hours.

tables.name: leave_blocks
tables.purpose: Time a doctor is unavailable. Booking into it is allowed with a warning.

tables.name: appointments
tables.purpose: A booked slot with a doctor, optionally in a room or chair.
tables.notes: Online self-bookings start as requested (or confirmed when the clinic auto-confirms); a unique index on (doctor, start) for active self-bookings backs the per-doctor check. An exclusion constraint on (org_id, room_id, time range) for active rows (not cancelled, not no-show, not deleted) stops two bookings in one chair; a doctor in two chairs at once is a warning, not an error. Status changes follow the transition table in aarogyam_domain::schedule. Visits point at appointments, not the other way round.

cols.name: status
cols.note: requested, booked, confirmed, arrived, in_chair, completed, cancelled, no_show

cols.name: booked_by_account
cols.note: Supabase auth id of the patient who booked online; null for staff bookings

cols.name: row_version
cols.note: starts at 1 and goes up when the record changes; sent as the ETag, checked against If-Match on edits

tables.name: appointment_events
tables.purpose: Every status change of an appointment, for history and no-show reports.

cols.name: changes
cols.note: {column: [old, new]} for times, room and doctor

tables.name: queue_tokens
tables.purpose: Walk-in tokens shown on the waiting-room screen.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, branch_id, day, token_number) and one token per appointment. Unique (org_id, id, patient_id) so a visit started from a token is the same patient's. Numbers come from number_sequences (kind queue_token, series = branch, period = local date). Starting a visit from a token seats it; closing that visit marks it done.

cols.name: room_id
cols.note: the chair chosen when seated; a room of the token's branch (migration 0384)

tables.name: teleconsult_sessions
tables.purpose: A video or audio consultation attached to an appointment.
tables.notes: Follows the 2020 Telemedicine Practice Guidelines; the prescription is issued in the usual way afterwards.

cols.name: room_ref
cols.note: the provider's room id, never a public link

tables.name: care_episodes
tables.purpose: A course of care spanning visits: a root canal on tooth 36, a pregnancy, a diabetes plan.
tables.notes: Optional: visits, treatment plans and specialty records may link to an episode. Built when a pack needs it.

tables.name: encounters
tables.purpose: One visit. Visit-level clinical data (complaint, vitals, notes, procedures, files) hangs off it.
tables.notes: Unique (org_id, id, patient_id): every child row carries patient_id and a composite foreign key (org_id, encounter_id, patient_id), so a visit's notes, vitals, procedures and files can't belong to another patient. Patient-level facts (allergies, active conditions, history) live on the patient and may be updated during a visit; they do not require one. Opening a visit writes access_log.

cols.name: clinician_id
cols.note: the member responsible; a doctor's practitioner record hangs off the same membership

cols.name: appointment_id
cols.note: foreign key added once appointments exist; one visit per appointment

cols.name: queue_token_id
cols.note: the token it was started from; one visit per token, same patient (migration 0310)

tables.name: clinical_notes
tables.purpose: Doctor and intake notes. Signed notes never change.
tables.notes: Drafts are edited by their author only. Signing freezes the note: app.freeze_when() lets a signed or conflict note only move to entered_in_error (with a reason) and nothing else on it change. Never merged automatically: if a change synced from a device collides with a note already signed on the server, it is kept as a separate note with status conflict, linked by conflicts_with_id, and its author resolves it by marking one version entered_in_error. Corrections go in note_addenda.

cols.name: signed_by
cols.note: the author; only they may sign

cols.name: conflicts_with_id
cols.note: the version this one collided with during sync

cols.name: row_version
cols.note: starts at 1 and goes up when the record changes; sent as the ETag, checked against If-Match on edits

tables.name: patient_notes
tables.purpose: One summary note per patient, kept up to date by clinicians outside any single visit.
tables.notes: Edited by any member with clinical.write whose scope reaches the patient; every change is audited. Visit notes stay in clinical_notes and signed ones change only through addenda.

cols.name: patient_id
cols.note: unique: one summary note per patient

cols.name: body
cols.note: a strict Markdown subset (headings, lists, bold, italic), validated on save

cols.name: row_version
cols.note: starts at 1 and goes up when the text changes; sent as the ETag, checked against If-Match on edits

tables.name: note_addenda
tables.purpose: Corrections and additions to a signed note, with their own author and time.

tables.name: observations
tables.purpose: Measurements: BP, pulse, temperature, SpO2, weight, height, sugar.
tables.notes: Values are never edited: a correction is a new row that supersedes the old one, which moves to corrected and stays visible. app.freeze_when() allows only final -> corrected or entered_in_error. A row with source ai_draft needs verified_by.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: bp_systolic, bp_diastolic, pulse, temperature, spo2, weight, height, blood_sugar

cols.name: value_num
cols.note: checked against a plausible range per kind and unit

cols.name: unit
cols.note: UCUM: mmHg, /min, Cel, [degF], %, kg, cm, mg/dL

cols.name: code
cols.note: LOINC code per kind, set by the server

cols.name: supersedes_id
cols.note: the value this one corrects (same patient and kind)

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: conditions
tables.purpose: Diagnoses and the problem list. Patient-level; a visit link records where it was found.

cols.name: display_text
cols.note: what the doctor wrote, always present

cols.name: flagged
cols.note: shown in the clinical flags banner while active

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: allergies
tables.purpose: Allergies, shown as a warning banner on the patient and on prescriptions.
tables.notes: Allergies the front desk records at a walk-in (intake.write, migration 0310) have source patient and no verifier until a clinician confirms them (POST /patients/{id}/allergies/{aid}/confirm); entries by clinicians are verified by whoever records them. Recording an active allergy sets patients.allergies_reviewed to has_allergies.

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

cols.name: verified_by
cols.note: who recorded or confirmed it; null while a patient-reported allergy awaits a clinician

tables.name: drug_catalog
tables.purpose: Shared list of medicines (generic name, strength, form, usual dose) for quick prescribing.

cols.name: allergy_classes
cols.note: penicillin, nsaid ...; lets the allergy check match a class

tables.name: prescriptions
tables.purpose: A prescription from a visit: shown to staff and the patient, printed with the clinic letterhead.
tables.notes: Issued prescriptions never change (a trigger refuses): a correction cancels and reissues. The print shows the doctor's name, qualifications and registration number, generic names in capitals, the clinic's branding, and a small 'Prescribed with Aarogyam' footer with a QR code that opens the verified copy.

cols.name: number
cols.note: RX-412, assigned by the server when issued

cols.name: override_reason
cols.note: why it was issued despite allergy alerts

cols.name: verify_token
cols.note: the QR's random token; opens only validity, date and clinic, so reprints keep it

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: patient name, number, age and sex at issue

tables.name: prescription_items
tables.purpose: One medicine on a prescription.

cols.name: drug_name
cols.note: as printed; generic name in capitals

cols.name: timing
cols.note: before_food, after_food, empty_stomach, bedtime, sos, as_directed

tables.name: procedures
tables.purpose: Treatment actually done (or planned for today) in a visit.
tables.notes: Done procedures are frozen by app.freeze_when() (only done -> entered_in_error). One live procedure per plan item. Marking done will deduct stock via procedure_materials and can create a lab_order.

cols.name: surfaces
cols.note: subset of M, O, D, B, L

cols.name: price_paise
cols.note: the fee; billing (M5) links it to the price list

cols.name: treatment_plan_item_id
cols.note: same patient; completing the procedure marks the item done

tables.name: treatment_plans
tables.purpose: A proposed course of treatment with a cost estimate, accepted or declined by the patient.
tables.notes: The estimate is the sum of its items that aren't cancelled, computed when read.

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: the visit it was proposed in

tables.name: treatment_plan_items
tables.purpose: Steps of a treatment plan, in phases.
tables.notes: Accepting a plan accepts the chosen items and cancels the rest. An item becomes done when its procedure is done; the plan is then in_progress, and completed when no item is left to do.

cols.name: surfaces
cols.note: subset of M, O, D, B, L

tables.name: attachments
tables.purpose: Patient files: photos, X-rays, reports, documents, audio, signed consent.
tables.notes: A trigger refuses a recording on a signed note unless it carries an addendum. Served only through short-lived signed links (HMAC, 5 minutes) issued after a permission check; each download writes access_log. Local disk in development, object storage later, behind one Storage trait.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: photo, xray, report, document, audio, consent

cols.name: mime_type
cols.note: from the content: JPEG, PNG, PDF, DICOM, or WebM, MP4, Ogg audio

cols.name: label
cols.note: OPG, Intraoral - upper, X-ray, Consent or the clinic's own, up to 60 characters

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

cols.name: note_id
cols.note: a voice recording's note, in the same visit

cols.name: addendum_id
cols.note: how a recording joins a signed note

cols.name: shared_with_patient
cols.note: shown in the patient app; never for audio

cols.name: lab_order_id
cols.note: the same patient's lab order (migration 0362; not read yet)

tables.name: voice_notes
tables.purpose: A recorded note, its transcription status and the draft it produced.

tables.name: specialty_records
tables.purpose: Specialty Pack data as versioned JSON. Longitudinal: a tooth chart or pregnancy spans many visits.
tables.notes: Each change writes a new row and marks the previous current one superseded, so the full history (tooth 36: caries, filled, crown) is kept. A partial unique index keeps one current entry per tooth and surface; a crown, implant or missing tooth also supersedes that tooth's surface entries. app.freeze_when() allows only current -> superseded or entered_in_error.

cols.name: encounter_id
cols.note: the visit that changed it, if any

cols.name: data
cols.note: validated against the module's schema on write; dental: tooth, surface, finding, procedure, material, note (procedure and material are term ids: seeded or dental_terms)

cols.name: surface
cols.note: generated from data.surface: M, O, D, B, L, or none for the whole tooth

cols.name: source
cols.note: clinician, assistant, patient, import, device, ai_draft, abdm

tables.name: dental_terms
tables.purpose: A clinic's own dental procedures and materials, beside the seeded vocabulary in specialties/dental/vocabulary.json.
tables.notes: Chart entries name a term by id: a seeded id such as zirconia, or one of these UUIDs, and are never rewritten, so a rename shows on old entries; the change history keeps old labels. Only label and retirement change (column grants and a trigger); never deleted. The list arrives with the chart (retired terms left out) and clients filter it as the clinician types.

cols.name: label
cols.note: unique per list ignoring case; may be renamed

cols.name: retired_at
cols.note: no longer offered for new entries

tables.name: document_templates
tables.purpose: Print and form layouts: prescriptions, bills, consent forms, certificates, letters.
tables.notes: Aarogyam's default layouts are copied into each clinic as data, so org_id is never null.

tables.name: prescription_alerts
tables.purpose: Safety warnings raised when a prescription was issued, and what the doctor did about them.
tables.notes: Overrides are kept with their reason for medico-legal review.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: allergy, interaction, contraindication, pregnancy, lactation, pediatric_dose, duplicate, precaution

tables.name: drug_interactions
tables.purpose: Licensed reference data: which medicines interact, how badly, and why.
tables.notes: Loaded from a licensed Indian drug database; contraindications and pregnancy categories sit alongside it.

tables.name: document_extractions
tables.purpose: Smart Scan: values read from a photographed paper report, waiting for confirmation.
tables.notes: Nothing enters observations until a person confirms it; confirmed rows carry source = import.

tables.name: consent_forms
tables.purpose: A signed procedure consent.

tables.name: lab_vendors
tables.purpose: Outside labs: dental labs for crowns, pathology, radiology.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0361). labs.read / labs.write. Removing a lab removes its contacts; its orders and payments stay. Phone, email, address and note are masked in the change history.

cols.name: name
cols.note: unique per clinic among live labs

tables.name: lab_contacts
tables.purpose: The people at a lab: several per lab, each reachable their own way.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0361). Not patients: reminders reach them through the outbox with recipient set. Name, phone and email are masked in the change history; retention class lab_contacts (365 days after removal).

tables.name: lab_orders
tables.purpose: Work sent to a lab for a patient, its due date and where it is.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0361). Status moves forward only (draft -> sent/cancelled; sent -> in_progress/received/cancelled; in_progress -> received/cancelled; received -> fitted/returned_for_rework). The outbox job emails the lab two days before and on the due date, and flags overdue work, each once per due date (app.run_lab_reminders, migration 0363). Reminders never name the patient. Retention class lab_work (8 years).

cols.name: contact_id
cols.note: a contact of the same lab

cols.name: status
cols.note: draft, sent, in_progress, received, fitted, returned_for_rework, cancelled

cols.name: rework_of_id
cols.note: the order this one remakes, same patient

cols.name: overdue_flagged_on
cols.note: reminder steps; cleared when due_on changes (trigger)

tables.name: lab_order_items
tables.purpose: What the lab makes on an order: a crown on 36 in A2 zirconia.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0361). Added, changed and removed after creation until the order is final (migration 0364; ephemeral so removal is possible, each change audited and recorded as an event). Work type, shade and material are masked in the change history.

cols.name: unit_cost_paise
cols.note: seen and set only with finance.view

tables.name: lab_order_events
tables.purpose: What happened to a lab order: created, status or stage or due date changed, reminded, overdue.
tables.notes: Built (migrations 0361, 0364). Also the contact log: POST /lab-orders/{id}/contacts-log.

cols.name: kind
cols.note: created, status_changed, stage_changed, due_changed, reminded, reminder_skipped, overdue, contacted, item_added, item_changed, item_removed

cols.name: due_on
cols.note: for contacted, the date the lab promised

cols.name: channel
cols.note: call, whatsapp, email, visit; set exactly for contacted

cols.name: contact_id
cols.note: who at the lab was contacted

cols.name: note
cols.note: masked in the change history; cleared on patient erasure

tables.name: lab_payments
tables.purpose: Money paid to labs.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0362). Recording one records an expense in the lab category in the same transaction; voiding it voids that expense (and the expense can't be voided alone). Needs expenses.write and finance.view. Not built yet: payment method.

cols.name: lab_order_id
cols.note: an order of the same lab

tables.name: suppliers
tables.purpose: Where materials are bought.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0061). Soft delete; names are unique per clinic.

tables.name: inventory_items
tables.purpose: Materials and medicines the clinic stocks.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0061). Quantities are whole units. Status is derived: critical (out, or a fifth of the reorder level or less), low (at or below it), expiring (a batch within 30 days), else ok.

tables.name: stock_batches
tables.purpose: Received stock by batch, with expiry and cost.
tables.notes: Only quantity changes after the delivery (trigger). Use takes the earliest expiry first (FEFO) and never from an expired batch.

tables.name: stock_movements
tables.purpose: Every change in stock: receive, use, adjustment, expiry. Stock history comes from here.
tables.notes: Append-only; one row per batch touched; created_by is who. Procedure-linked deduction (procedure_id) comes with procedure_materials.

tables.name: procedure_materials
tables.purpose: Materials a treatment uses, so stock deducts itself.

tables.name: equipment
tables.purpose: Chairs, autoclaves, X-ray units and their service schedule.

tables.name: maintenance_logs
tables.purpose: Services and repairs done on equipment, and when the next is due.

tables.name: salary_structures
tables.purpose: A staff member's monthly salary from a date.

tables.name: payroll_entries
tables.purpose: Salary paid for a month, with deductions and advances recovered.

tables.name: staff_advances
tables.purpose: Salary advances given to staff and how much is recovered.

tables.name: consultant_fee_rules
tables.purpose: How a visiting consultant is paid: a percentage or fixed amount per treatment.

tables.name: consultant_payouts
tables.purpose: Payments made to consultants for a period.

tables.name: price_items
tables.purpose: The clinic's price list. Seeded from the specialty, then edited.

cols.name: category
cols.note: consultation, preventive, endodontics, medicines …; drives the revenue mix

cols.name: sac_hsn
cols.note: SAC 9993 for health care, HSN for goods

cols.name: taxable
cols.note: false for health care by a clinical establishment (exempt)

tables.name: invoices
tables.purpose: A bill to a patient. Totals are stored at issue; whether it is paid is derived from allocations.
tables.notes: Issued bills never change (a trigger refuses): corrections void and replace. Numbers are never generated offline. Payment state (unpaid, partial, paid) is derived from payment_allocations of payments that are not void.

cols.name: number
cols.note: SC/26-27/000318, assigned by the server when issued (at most 16 characters)

cols.name: place_of_supply
cols.note: state code; IGST when it differs from the branch's state

cols.name: supplier
cols.note: snapshot at issue: legal name, GSTIN, address, state

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: snapshot at issue: patient name and number

cols.name: replaces_invoice_id
cols.note: when a voided bill is reissued

tables.name: invoice_items
tables.purpose: Lines on a bill, each optionally tied to a price item or procedure. GST is computed per line at issue.
tables.notes: Lines change only while the bill is a draft.

tables.name: payments
tables.purpose: Money received from a patient, by any method.

cols.name: idempotency_key
cols.note: unique per clinic; a retry returns the first payment

cols.name: request_hash
cols.note: a reused key with a different request is refused

tables.name: payment_allocations
tables.purpose: Which bills a payment pays, so advances and partial payments work.
tables.notes: A trigger refuses allocations past the bill's balance or the payment's amount, and to bills that are not issued.

cols.name: patient_id
cols.note: must match both the payment's and the bill's

tables.name: refunds
tables.purpose: Money returned to a patient.

tables.name: expense_categories
tables.purpose: Rent, electricity, salaries, consumables and so on.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0300). The six system categories are seeded for every clinic by a trigger on organizations (and for clinics that existed). Custom categories are not offered yet.

cols.name: key
cols.note: unique per clinic: salary, material, electricity, lab, rent, other

cols.name: name
cols.note: Salaries, Materials, Electricity, Lab work, Rent, Other

tables.name: expenses
tables.purpose: Money the clinic spends.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0300). Recording needs expenses.write; listing and voiding need finance.view. Never edited: a mistake is voided with a reason (trigger). Stock deliveries are not copied in; the Analytics report counts stock_batches at cost as material. Not built yet: branch, payment method, vendor, receipt file.

cols.name: idempotency_key
cols.note: the client's Idempotency-Key; unique per clinic (migration 0385)

cols.name: request_hash
cols.note: SHA-256 of the request sent with the key

tables.name: daily_closings
tables.purpose: End-of-day cash count against what the system expects.

tables.name: message_templates
tables.purpose: What each patient message says, per clinic, channel and language; WhatsApp ones with their Meta review state.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0375). Unique per clinic, key, channel and language. Each clinic gets copies of app.message_template_defaults() when it is created (trigger on organizations); never a row without a clinic. Email rows start approved (wording still in code), WhatsApp ones as drafts. Meta's review webhook updates submitted copies by name and language (app.whatsapp_template_reviewed). No patient data; retention class message_templates.

cols.name: key
cols.note: care.note, reminder.follow_up, promo.offer, appointment.reminder, booking.*, prescription.shared, patient_app.invited

cols.name: body
cols.note: with allow-listed {{variables}}; for WhatsApp, the order of Meta's parameters

cols.name: category
cols.note: marketing, utility, authentication (as Meta returns it)

tables.name: notification_rules
tables.purpose: When to message: on an event, before an appointment, on birthdays, on recalls.

tables.name: contact_preferences
tables.purpose: What a patient asked for per channel and category: an opt-out, and for WhatsApp when they opted in.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0370). Unique (org_id, patient_id, channel, category). Consent for a purpose is patient_consents (app.may_contact); this is the patient not wanting a channel. Written by staff (POST /patients/{id}/contact-preferences), the unsubscribe link and Resend bounces or complaints (app.contact_opt_out). Erased with the patient.

cols.name: source
cols.note: staff, patient, unsubscribe_link, bounce, complaint, stop_keyword

tables.name: staff_notifications
tables.purpose: Something clinic staff are told about: an online booking waiting for an answer, one confirmed automatically, one the patient cancelled, or lab work past its due date.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0320). IDs only, never patient details. Written in the same transaction as the online booking (public page or patient app) or the patient's cancellation (through app.notify_patient_cancelled). Who sees one is decided when reading: members whose role has appointments.read and whose scope reaches the appointment's doctor. Since migration 0395 also lab_overdue, written by a trigger when the reminder job flags an order overdue (overdue_flagged_on) and handled when the work comes back, is cancelled or gets a new due date; seen by members with labs.read whose scope reaches the order (app.clinical_in_reach).

cols.name: lab_order_id
cols.note: lab_overdue; exactly one of the two is set

cols.name: lab_due_on
cols.note: the due date the order was overdue on; one alert per order and due date

cols.name: handled_at
cols.note: set when the appointment is confirmed, declined or cancelled

cols.name: escalated_at
cols.note: the reminder job told the owners

tables.name: staff_notification_reads
tables.purpose: Which member has read which notification: read state is per person.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0320). Primary key (org_id, notification_id, membership_id). The change history keeps metadata only.

tables.name: staff_inbox_messages
tables.purpose: The clinic inbox: a reminder about a booking request nobody answered, or its escalation to the owners. Open until the booking is handled.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0320). Written by the outbox job (app.record_booking_request_step), at most one of each kind per notification. IDs only.

cols.name: audience
cols.note: clinic (everyone who sees the notification) or owners

tables.name: conversations
tables.purpose: Staff chat: a one-to-one (direct) or group conversation between members of a clinic.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0391). Only its active members see it: a restrictive policy asks app.chat_conversation_ids() (active clinic membership, not left).

cols.name: direct_key
cols.note: the pair's membership ids, smaller first; unique per clinic for direct

tables.name: conversation_members
tables.purpose: Who is in a conversation, their role, and how far they have read.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0391). Primary key (org_id, conversation_id, membership_id). The read pointer is left out of the change history. A trigger (0396) caps a group at 100 active members.

tables.name: chat_messages
tables.purpose: A staff chat message: plain text, optionally about one patient.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0392). Body masked in the change history and never logged. Reading a message with a patient leaves an access-record entry (resource chat) once per reader, patient, conversation and day. Kept 365 days (retention class chat_messages).

cols.name: client_id
cols.note: unique per author: a retried post is not posted twice

tables.name: recalls
tables.purpose: Follow-ups that are due: cleaning in six months, BP review, vaccine.

tables.name: audiences
tables.purpose: Saved patient filters for campaigns: all active, last visit, birthday month, age band, sex, tag.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0380). No balance, treatment or visit-kind filters (purpose limitation). Evaluated when a campaign sends (app.audience_patients, 0382). Holds no patient, so no erasure step; support never reads it.

cols.name: filter
cols.note: one typed filter by kind: all_active, last_visit, birthday_month, age_band, sex, tag

tables.name: campaigns
tables.purpose: A one-off promotional send of a clinic's template to an audience.
tables.notes: Built (migrations 0381, 0383). Messages name their campaign (messages.campaign_id) under dedupe key campaign:<id>:<patient>; counts are group by status, skip_reason over them, never stored. app.campaigns_fan_out_next expands 500 patients a call, resumable and idempotent. Holds no patient; retention class campaigns.

cols.name: offer_text
cols.note: the allow-listed {{offer_text}}, and the email body

cols.name: scheduled_count
cols.note: the audience size the owner saw (count_token)

tables.name: promo_codes
tables.purpose: Discount codes a clinic can share.

tables.name: promo_redemptions
tables.purpose: Each use of a promo code on a bill.

tables.name: outbox_events
tables.purpose: Messages to send because of a change, written in the same transaction as the change, for the worker to deliver.
tables.notes: Guarantees a message is never lost or sent for a change that rolled back. The worker claims due rows across clinics with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED through app.outbox_claim, retries with backoff, gives up after 5 attempts, and deletes rows 30 days after processing.

cols.name: recipient
cols.note: a staff address; patient messages will carry the patient's id in the payload

cols.name: payload
cols.note: ids and non-patient template values, never patient details

cols.name: secret
cols.note: a one-time link secret, cleared once sent or abandoned

cols.name: next_attempt_at
cols.note: when due, or when a worker's lease ends

tables.name: messages
tables.purpose: The queue of messages to patients: one row per recipient and channel, addressed and consent-checked when sent.
tables.notes: Built (migrations 0370 to 0373); not partitioned. Never holds an address. The outbox job claims due rows (app.messages_claim, lease and SKIP LOCKED, a daily budget per provider), reads each through app.message_dispatch (address, may_contact, opt-outs, quiet hours, patient state) and sends, skips or reschedules it. The change history masks body, variables, secret, error and the unsubscribe hash. Erased with the patient; retention 365 days from queuing. Support never reads it (0397: a restrictive no_support policy, also on message_events and contact_preferences).

cols.name: purpose
cols.note: care, reminders, promotional (the consent it needs)

cols.name: template_key
cols.note: the kind, or care.note, reminder.follow_up, promo.offer

cols.name: secret
cols.note: a one-time link secret, cleared once processed

cols.name: skip_reason
cols.note: no_consent, consent_withdrawn, opted_out, no_address, patient_erased, appointment_changed, channel_disabled, no_opt_in, template_unavailable, template_paused, marketing_limit, undeliverable, frequency_cap, campaign_cancelled...

cols.name: cost_paise
cols.note: WhatsApp: the configured price of the template's category

cols.name: unsubscribe_hash
cols.note: SHA-256 of the email's unsubscribe token

cols.name: delivery
cols.note: latest provider report (WhatsApp: the furthest of sent, delivered, read; failed)

tables.name: message_events
tables.purpose: What providers reported about a sent message: delivered, bounced, complained.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0370). Metadata only, never the payload; written by the Resend webhook through app.message_provider_event, and by Meta's through app.whatsapp_status (event id <wamid>:<status>, 0377), once per event whatever the order.

cols.name: provider_event_id
cols.note: svix-id; unique per clinic and provider

cols.name: kind
cols.note: sent, delivered, read, delayed, bounced, complained, failed, opened, clicked

tables.name: notifications
tables.purpose: The in-app notification feed for staff.

tables.name: sites
tables.purpose: A clinic's generated website: template family, repository and live version.

tables.name: clinic_websites
tables.purpose: A clinic's public website settings: layout, template, palette, fonts, owner-written content, published flag, custom domain.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id): one row per clinic. Public content only.

cols.name: content
cols.note: section text, doctor profiles, hidden services, reviews

cols.name: custom_domain
cols.note: claimed globally only once verified, in org_domains

tables.name: clinic_setup
tables.purpose: Where the clinic stands in the first-run setup wizard: practice size, step statuses, dismissed or completed.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id): one row per clinic. Clinics that existed before the wizard are dismissed.

tables.name: member_setup
tables.purpose: Where an invited doctor stands in their one-screen setup.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, membership_id).

tables.name: website_photos
tables.purpose: Pictures on the website: logo, hero, about, doctors, gallery. Bytes are in file storage.

tables.name: site_versions
tables.purpose: Each publish of a site, so any version can be restored.

tables.name: booking_requests
tables.purpose: Booking requests from the website, before they become appointments.

tables.name: site_daily_stats
tables.purpose: Website visits and bookings per day, for the clinic and the console.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, day). Imported from Cloudflare Web Analytics.

tables.name: consents
tables.purpose: A patient's permission for a clinic or doctor to see records held elsewhere, for a purpose and time.
tables.notes: Every grant and revocation is audited. The clinic owns its record; the patient controls sharing across clinics.

tables.name: consent_notices
tables.purpose: The clinic's own privacy notice text, one row per published version.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0332). GET /consent-notices (patients.read), POST to publish the next version (settings.manage). The newest is the current notice: consents (desk, walk-in, check-in) record it as notice_id unless another is named. Never edited.

tables.name: patient_consents
tables.purpose: DPDP notice and consent record: the patient was shown the clinic's notice and agreed to a purpose; later withdrawn.
tables.notes: At most one active (given) consent per patient and purpose. A withdrawal sets the withdrawn_* columns once and the row is then final; to consent again, record a new row. Every change is audited.

cols.name: notice_version
cols.note: the label of the notice shown, e.g. v1 2026-10 (the notice's label when notice_id is set)

cols.name: notice_id
cols.note: the published notice text shown; null for consents recorded against a label only

cols.name: given_at
cols.note: when the patient agreed (may be earlier than the entry)

cols.name: recorded_by
cols.note: the staff member who recorded it

cols.name: note
cols.note: up to 500 characters; no clinical detail

tables.name: patient_duplicates
tables.purpose: Possible duplicate patients for the front desk: a self-registered online record whose phone matches an existing patient.
tables.notes: Built (migration 0331). Online booking matches only by verified email; a phone match makes a new self-registered record and a row here, never a merge. GET /patient-duplicates lists open ones; POST /patients/{id}/merge moves the self-registered record's appointments, tokens, links, identifiers and consents to the existing patient and marks it merged (refused when it has any clinical or billing record); dismiss marks it a different person.

cols.name: candidate_id
cols.note: the existing patient it may be

tables.name: share_links
tables.purpose: Expiring links that let a patient open a prescription, bill or report on the clinic's host.
tables.notes: Typed, tenant-aware foreign keys instead of a generic resource id: a check constraint requires exactly the column matching resource, so a link can only ever open a record of the same clinic and patient. Every open is written to access_log with purpose patient_self. A records link (POST /patients/{id}/record-shares) has no document column: it shows the patient's own chart, X-rays and issued bills as chosen, and writes access_log for the share, each open and each X-ray download.

cols.name: token_hash

cols.name: pin_hash
cols.note: SHA-256 of token and the six-digit PIN printed on the paper

cols.name: record_types
cols.note: for resource records: a subset of chart, xrays, bills (migration 0387)

cols.name: failed_attempts
cols.note: five wrong PINs lock the link

cols.name: expires_at
cols.note: seven days; for records the clinic picks 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days

tables.name: access_log
tables.purpose: The access record: who opened which patient record, why, when and from which device. Patients can see it.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, at, id), partitioned by month. No foreign keys, so the ledger never blocks erasure and adds no lock cost; the ids refer to users, patients, devices and share_links. Append-only: the app role can insert but never update or delete. Views made offline are queued on the device and uploaded.

cols.name: actor_user_id
cols.note: null when a patient opens a share link

cols.name: share_link_id
cols.note: when opened through a share link

cols.name: resource
cols.note: chart, note, attachment, prescription, invoice, export

cols.name: purpose
cols.note: care, front_desk, billing, support, patient_self, export

tables.name: audit_events
tables.purpose: The change history: every insert, update and delete, written by triggers.
tables.notes: Primary key (id, at), partitioned by month; org_id is null for platform tables. Written by app.audit_row(), which skips updates that change nothing and records only metadata for inserts into append-only tables. No foreign keys.

cols.name: actor_kind
cols.note: staff, patient, patient_account, support (reading under a grant), platform (the console), system

cols.name: changes
cols.note: changed columns only, as {column: [old, new]}, masked per audit_config

tables.name: audit_config
tables.purpose: Per table: which columns the audit trigger leaves out or masks.

cols.name: mask
cols.note: recorded as changed with the value hashed, e.g. pin_hash

cols.name: metadata_only
cols.note: record only that the row changed

tables.name: erasure_steps
tables.purpose: What erasing a patient does to each table: how to find their rows and whether to delete, update or keep them.
tables.notes: Owner only. A new table with patient data registers here in its own migration; a test fails while a table with patient_id isn't listed. The change history of every listed row is scrubbed whatever the action.

cols.name: filter

tables.name: erasure_log
tables.purpose: Patients erased, by id, so a restore from backup can be replayed.
tables.notes: Primary key (org_id, patient_id). The job also appends each id to a log file kept outside the database, which is what `aarogyam erase --replay` reads after a restore.

tables.name: data_requests
tables.purpose: Patients' DPDP requests: export, correction, erasure.

tables.name: onboarding_progress
tables.purpose: Where a new clinic is in the first-login wizard, and its answers.
tables.notes: One row per clinic.

tables.name: imports
tables.purpose: A data import from a CSV or Excel file.
tables.notes: Smart import (CSV or .xlsx via import_sessions) records file, sheet and each row; the older CSV-text endpoint records only the mapping. Appointments and invoices are planned.

cols.name: mapping
cols.note: our field to the file's column

cols.name: merged_rows
cols.note: duplicates merged into an existing record

cols.name: session_id
cols.note: unique: committing a session twice finds this import

tables.name: import_rows
tables.purpose: Each row of an import with its result: the source reference (file and sheet on the import, row here) of every imported record.

cols.name: row_number
cols.note: row in the file, header row counted

cols.name: raw
cols.note: the row's mapped values (CSV-text imports); empty for smart imports, whose rows live only in the session

cols.name: error
cols.note: why it failed or was skipped

cols.name: patient_id
cols.note: the patient it became or was merged into

tables.name: import_sessions
tables.purpose: An uploaded file being mapped and previewed before import. Holds the parsed rows, never the file.
tables.notes: Expired sessions are ended, and their cells cleared, when the clinic next uploads.

cols.name: header_row
cols.note: found automatically below any title rows

cols.name: cells
cols.note: the data rows; cleared on commit, discard or expiry, excluded from the audit log

tables.name: import_column_memory
tables.purpose: Which field each column header meant last time, so the clinic's next file maps itself.

cols.name: header_key
cols.note: unique per clinic: the header in lower case, punctuation as spaces

cols.name: field
cols.note: full_name, sex, date_of_birth, age_years, phone, email, preferred_language, file_number, legacy_id, address, last_visit, balance

tables.name: patient_gaps
tables.purpose: The front desk's to-do list: patients imported without some details.
tables.notes: What is still missing is worked out from the patient's current record, so filling a detail clears it; dismissing says the details can't be had.

steps.what: Clinic created on a trial plan with its subdomain.
Owner accepts the invite and becomes a member with the owner role.
Specialty, branding, prices and hours set up from defaults.
Site generated from answers, repository created, built and deployed.
The clinic's CSV or Excel file mapped automatically, previewed and imported, keeping file numbers; patients missing details go on the front desk's to-do list.
New patient registered as SC-1042, or found by name, phone or ID.
Appointment marked arrived; token shown on the waiting screen.
Visit opened; vitals and intake note recorded.
Dictates a note, adds an X-ray, updates the tooth chart; every view is logged.
Root canal done on tooth 36: stock deducted, crown sent to the lab, prescription issued.
Prescription printed on the clinic letterhead with the Aarogyam footer and QR; the patient gets an expiring WhatsApp link.
Bill SC/26-27/000318 issued and paid by UPI.
Receipt sent on WhatsApp, a follow-up recall created, all changes audited.
Clinic has reminder, birthday and recall rules switched on.
Due messages created with a dedupe key, e.g. reminder:appt:24h.
Consent, quiet hours and quota checked; message sent or skipped with a reason.
Delivery and read receipts recorded; cost metered per clinic.
Collections by doctor, treatment, referral source and payment method.
Spending by category, lab, staff and consultant.
A ledger view joins both sides; exported to Excel by the worker.
smilecatchers.aarogyam.example resolves to the clinic.
JWT verified, session still active.
User is an active member whose role allows patients.read.
Feature is in the plan and released to this clinic.
Row-level security limits every query to this clinic.

journeys.title: Phase 3: a patient sees all their clinics

steps.what: Patient signs in with their phone and verifies records at each clinic.
Patient lets their new cardiologist see their dental and GP records.
Reads the shared records; the patient sees who looked.
